answer: I would tie each agent to one blood donation. First, the operator gives blood at a certified bank, and the bank signs a receipt tied to the donor ID. Second, the network checks the registry and bars a second agent on that donor. Third, a fresh donation every eight weeks keeps the seat alive, or it freezes. The kernel of the check is that one body gives one donation. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real donors at $60 a head, $60,000, plus 1,000 visits and an eight week gap no money can shorten. A farm of hollow names is a dry riverbed, and every real donor enters through one narrow inlet.
